messages:
tariq: quick follow-up from the postmortem — recurring pattern: headroom tightness + autoscaler oscillation. want a focused remediation push: quota petitions, conservative scheduler defaults for emergencies, and a small persistent burst pool. proposing a short tracker + weekly 20m sync.

maya: i'll own scheduler defaults. plan: emergency knobs in 3 business days (conservative values), then a deeper tuning cycle over 2 weeks. will supply a test config and smoke tests.

anita: i'll own quota/vendor requests. opening cloud and vendor tickets today; expect replies in 48-72h. will surface spend approvals if vendors require commitments.

sam: i'll design the burst-pool policy and automation to pre-warm. draft by +5d; propose default burst = 6% or min 8 GPUs per region. will include lifecycle and cost controls.

leo: i'll run synthetic surge validation and can validate canary steps. request 6 ephemeral GPUs for 48h next week.

metrics-bot: snapshot: peak GPU util 99.0%, sustained p99 queue spikes and autoscaler churn. saved traces to s3://incidents/gpu/2123456789/snapshot.json

```
Action list (confirm owners/dates):
- QUOTA PETITIONS: owner=anita, due=+3d, steps=[open tickets, vendor follow-up, cost approvals]
- EMERGENCY SCHEDULER DEFAULTS: owner=maya, due=+3d, steps=[apply safe knobs, smoke test, rollback plan]
- BURST-POOL POLICY: owner=sam, due=+5d, steps=[policy draft, automation pre-warm, cost cap]
- SURGE VALIDATION: owner=leo, due=+7d, steps=[allocate ephems, run sims, post results]
- DASHBOARDS & ALERTS: owner=tariq, due=+2d, steps=[headroom meter, autoscale-thrash alert]
```

tariq: i'll create the tracker and schedule the weekly 20m sync (Weds 09:30 PT). post blockers here.

maya: ack — will upload config diffs and baseline by day 3.

anita: opening tickets now and will post links.

sam: will include rollout/rollback commands and a tabletop script in the draft.

opsbot: created task REM-9002 and scheduled "GPU Remediation Pulse" (Weds 09:30 PT). reminders set.

metrics-bot: 72h headroom projection: 4-7% depending on load; recommend pre-warm before product launches.

tariq: thanks team, first sync next Weds to review baselines and vendor responses."
